LESSON: READING 13.4.1 ORAL LITERATURE: PRAISE SONGS

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 13
Topic 13.4: Reading 13.4.1 Oral Literature: Praise Songs
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Reading 13.4.1 Oral Literature: Praise Songs, part of Strand 13 in Grade 7 ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: Why do we sing? 2. What are the qualities of a good singer?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify the purpose and occasions for which praise songs are performed,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 13.4.1 Oral Literature: Praise Songs in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. discuss the relationship between the singer and the person being praised in praise songs,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 13.4.1 Oral Literature: Praise Songs in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. perform praise songs sung in their immediate environment,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 13.4.1 Oral Literature: Praise Songs in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. collaborate with peers in performing the praise songs,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 13.4.1 Oral Literature: Praise Songs in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

E. appreciate the purpose of praise songs in communication.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 13.4.1 Oral Literature: Praise Songs in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. identify the purpose and occasions for which praise songs are performed,

   Reading 13.4.1 Oral Literature: Praise Songs helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. discuss the relationship between the singer and the person being praised in praise songs,

   Reading 13.4.1 Oral Literature: Praise Songs helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. perform praise songs sung in their immediate environment,

   Reading 13.4.1 Oral Literature: Praise Songs helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. collaborate with peers in performing the praise songs,

   Reading 13.4.1 Oral Literature: Praise Songs helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

E. appreciate the purpose of praise songs in communication.

   Reading 13.4.1 Oral Literature: Praise Songs helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

F. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. listen to praise songs from audio-visual sources or from a resource person,

2. identify and discuss the purpose of the praise songs they have listened to,

3. share ideas on the relationship between the singer and the person been praised in the praise songs they have listened to,

4. identify a praise song sang in their immediate environment,

5. collaborate to present praise songs to the class and share experiences,

6. discuss the character traits of the singer(s) as brought out in the praise song(s). 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. listen to praise songs from audio-visual sources or from a resource person,
2. identify and discuss the purpose of the praise songs they have listened to,
3. share ideas on the relationship between the singer and the person been praised in the praise songs they have listened to,
4. identify a praise song sang in their immediate environment,
5. collaborate to present praise songs to the class and share experiences,
6. discuss the character traits of the singer(s) as brought out in the praise song(s). 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Reading 13.4.1 Oral Literature: Praise Songs together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Self-efficacy: It is strengthened as the learner shares ideas on the relationship between the singer and the person being

praised in a praise song.

• Creativity and imagination: It is enhanced as the learner gains new perspectives on how to do things as they collaborate to

present praise songs to the class and share experiences.

Values:
Respect is enhanced as the learner values human dignity while collaborating with peers to perform praise songs.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs)

Life skills: The skill of living with others is inculcated as the learner identifies and performs praise songs.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner relates performance skills to other learning areas such as Creative Arts and Sports.

Main points to remember:

1. identify the purpose and occasions for which praise songs are performed,
2. discuss the relationship between the singer and the person being praised in praise songs,
3. perform praise songs sung in their immediate environment,
4. collaborate with peers in performing the praise songs,
5. appreciate the purpose of praise songs in communication.

Remember the key question: Why do we sing? 2. What are the qualities of a good singer?
